Hi everyone and welcome back to the Aesthetic and Wellness Edge. I'm your host, Bethany Gifford, and this is the show where we dive into real world stories, strategies, and challenges of leaders shaping the aesthetic and wellness industry. Today we're welcomed by a true visionary in the Med Spa acquisition space. But first, a word from our sponsor.

Bethany Gifford (00:25.482)
Today I am thrilled to be joined by Lisa Bell, founder and CEO of Amara. Lisa comes from an incredible background spanning Fortune 100 companies, finance, growth strategy, and health tech startups. She has pivoted into aesthetics with a very unique approach to acquiring and building med spas. Her company Amara is creating sustainable growth of all med spas across multiple states with a twist.

Instead of rolling everything under one brand, Lisa is committed to helping each practice remain hyper local, patient first, and rooted into its community. Lisa, welcome to the show.

Thank you, Bethany, very happy to be here.

I fell in love with med spas. It was actually after I started into this endeavor because early on I was not terribly familiar with the med spa space, but the first med spa that I visited is when things really clicked for me. I think my largest takeaway was everybody here is happy.

I was just sitting in the med spa that we were looking to acquire, that one we actually did acquire, and clients were coming in just so happy, leaving so happy, and the providers were so happy. And having been in, I don't know, 10 plus industries, I have never seen anything like that. And that's kind of what solidified it for me. Is that kind of what drew you into the small business aspect of things?

But at the end of the day,

I started to realize I just don't care. And I don't feel like I'm making a very big impact. I was working effectively nonstop, making a lot of decisions, working with some really smart people, but I didn't feel like I could really see the impact of what I was doing. And...

Yeah.

you guys hit the sweet spot right in the middle. That's great. Could you kind of walk us a little bit about like how you identify and acquire these practices?

my.
